To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between biodiversity and ecosystem functioning is scale dependent.

(1) species richness, ecological function, and ecological resilience are scale dependent; (2) species interact with scale-dependent sets of ecological structures; and (3) ecological resilience is generated when species interact with scale-specific sets of structures and processes.
(1) species richness is positively associated with the number of functional groups, and (2) the number of functional group is positively associated with ecological resilience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the diversity of ecological structures and ecological processes, and their interactions, contribute to resilience and to the maintenance of ecosystem functions.
the relationship between ecological diversity and ecological resilience.
the role of scale, species diversity, and ecological resilience in maintaining the functional integrity of ecological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diversity of life on Earth is the result of a process of evolution that has occurred over billions of years, and that this process has produced a vast array of species that are all interrelated in a complex web of interactions and interdependencies.
biodiversity is the key to resilience and the key to the resilience of biodiversity is scale.
the diversity of ecological structures and the distribution of functional processes across scales generate resilience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new conceptual framework for the study of biodiversity that is more comprehensive than previous frameworks.

we are attempting to develop an ecological theory that is based on the notion that the distribution of species across scales of space and time generates the functional diversity that is necessary for ecological resilience.
the distribution of species richness and ecological resilience across scales is the key to the long-term maintenance of ecological integrity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ecological resilience is not a single entity but is distributed across scales.
the relationship between biodiversity and ecological resilience is complex and scale dependent.
ecological resilience is not a property of species, but of species in the context of scale.
